summary: Draws a Lucide icon at a token size with the system stroke width, in the color of the text around it. Decorative by default: pass a label only when the icon carries meaning on its own.
whenToUse: Next to a label, to help people scan: a menu item, a tab, a status line, a table cell.
Inside your own controls, at size sm (16), the size the system uses in controls.
In navigation at size md (20), so the side nav reads at a glance.
Any Lucide glyph: pass the component itself, for example icon={GitBranch} imported from lucide-react.
whenNotToUse: As the only content of a button: use IconButton, which requires a label and sizes the hit area.
Inside Button or Badge when they place the icon for you: Button takes iconStart and iconEnd, Badge takes icon.
Emoji or Unicode glyphs standing in for icons: the system uses one family, Lucide.
Illustrations or logos: Icon draws 24px grid line icons only.

dos.title: Pair the icon with text
dos.text: The word carries the meaning and the icon helps people find it. The icon stays hidden from screen readers, so the label is read once.

dos.title: Pick the size from the token scale
dos.text: xs 12, sm 16, md 20, lg 24. The stroke stays at icon.stroke on every size, so icons keep the weight of the text.

dos.title: Give a label when the icon stands alone and means something
dos.text: With label, Icon becomes role="img" with that accessible name. Say what it means ("Merged"), not what it shows ("Purple circle").

donts.title: Set a color or a size by hand
donts.text: Icon inherits currentColor and takes its size from the icon size tokens. A hard-coded width or color drifts from the theme and the density.

donts.title: Rely on the icon alone to say a status
donts.text: Color and shape are not enough for everyone. Put the status in words next to it, or use Badge.

accessibility: Without label, the icon gets aria-hidden="true": screen readers skip it and read the text next to it.
With label, it gets role="img" and aria-label, so it is announced as an image with that name.
focusable="false" keeps the SVG out of the tab order. Make the parent control focusable, never the icon.
The icon inherits the text color, so it gets the same contrast as the label it sits next to.
contentGuidelines: A label names the meaning in sentence case: "Merged", "Opens in a new tab".
Do not add "icon" or "image" to the label: screen readers already announce the role.
